pull_request.title: Infrastructure: Activate nODD specialist roles and workflow skills
pull_request.head: codex/agent-workflow
pull_request.body:
nODD's eight specialist roles were documented but had no reusable execution profiles or common assignment procedure. This PR connects those mandates to on-demand delegation: small dependent changes stay with the main agent; substantial work receives bounded specialist assignments and revision-specific handoffs.

## Change

- Add eight project-scoped role profiles and three discoverable workflow skills for coordination, design evidence, and review/validation.
- Add a Python 3.11+ standard-library helper that validates assignment contracts and emits explicit role prompts with verified Git source locators. It starts no agents and changes no permissions.
- Add delegation rules to AGENTS.md, a [usage guide](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/codex/agent-workflow/docs/AGENT_WORKFLOW.md), and CI checks.
- Retain assignments, findings and limitations in the existing session journal; infrastructure remains excluded from scientific progress tracking.

## Pilot and limits

TrackTech and SysArch assessed existing DES-020 inputs in separate contexts; PhysVal independently assessed primary scientific evidence. The coordinator reconciled the inherited endcap schedule against the later DES-021 amendment and retained source-identity and qualification limits. All three used the same full source revision and changed no scientific files.

The [pilot record](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/codex/agent-workflow/logs/codex/SESSION-2026-10-12-agent-workflow.md#delegation-pilot) documents exact contracts, cited outcomes and actual checks. Explicit role instructions were exercised. Native custom-profile selection remains unverified because this chat's delegation tool exposes no profile-selection field. Local CLI discovery of all three skills was verified. Exact counters for this task and its children were unavailable and were not estimated.

## Validation

- [x] 85 Python tests passed: 14 assignment controls, 28 project records, 33 session logging, 10 token dashboard.
- [x] All three skills passed the skill-creator validator.
- [x] Workflow assets, 169 session pairs, and existing scientific records validated.
- [x] Token-dashboard preview build and chart interaction checks passed.
- [x] Local links/headings, infrastructure PR classification, whitespace and unchanged scientific sources checked.
- [x] Human approval boundaries preserved; no detector/design lifecycle changes or infrastructure progress entries.

Governance: existing development-plan role mandates and ADR-004 logging policy. DES-020, DES-021 and DES-010 are read-only pilot inputs. No new design sign-off is requested by this infrastructure change.

The user asked whether nODD's documented roles were active agents, discussed
role profiles and reusable skills with agents started for bounded work, then
requested: “Prepare this infrastructure PR as suggested.” The agreed deliverable
includes eight role profiles, three reusable procedures, delegation rules,
assignment/handoff guidance and a documented pilot. It does not request continuous
background operation, external messages, detector changes or human sign-off.

The starting revision is `ed30e63fb0ab30b66d4084a9058906929006f792`, current
`origin/main` after fetch, on new branch `codex/agent-workflow`. The isolated
worktree started clean. The existing nODD checkout's unrelated changes were
preserved. The app worktree tool initially selected the parent workspace's Git
repository and could not resolve `origin/main`; a dedicated nODD Git worktree
was created instead. Initial sandboxed network/Git operations needed the
normal escalation path; their authorized retries succeeded.

The branch was pushed normally and
[draft PR #68](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/pull/68) was opened against
`main` with title `Infrastructure: Activate nODD specialist roles and workflow skills`.
The GitHub connector returned HTTP 403 (integration lacks creation permission);
the existing authenticated GitHub CLI successfully created the PR using the
exact body file. The PR was attached to this chat. No external messages,
reviewer pings, merge, deployment or recurring jobs were requested or performed.

At creation inspection, the PR head was `e3395c263fc6bb2ccef9a9160595eaae1aca7de8`; project validation
and token-site hosted checks were IN_PROGRESS. Local checks are reported
separately. Follow later check state in the PR; this observation does not claim
hosted success. The final logging commit records closeout without a self-referential
hash; Git history identifies that enclosing revision.

The infrastructure deliverable and explicit-dispatch pilot are complete. Native
profile selection remains unverified and current-task token coverage remains
unknown. Scientific qualification questions and source reconciliation observed
in the pilot are retained for future project tasks, not silently implemented here.
